title: Does the thinking really do the work?
blurb: We turn the thinking down, round by round, and break other parts on purpose, to see whether the answers fall with it.

scenes.heading: Where we are: the thinker

caption.text: This part is the thinker, a team of note-takers that works in rounds.
We claim the thinking does the work. This chapter tests that claim.

scenes.note: One round = one lap: look at the whole question, pass notes, think.

scenes.heading: More rounds: no gain

caption.text: Now turn the dial past its practice, to 24 rounds.
The score does not rise: 72.57, which is 27 fewer right (4,410 minus 4,383).
The design we plan to ship adds a learned stop switch, which picks the number of rounds.

1 round: 0.0. 2 rounds: 1.1. 12 and 24 rounds: 99.9.

scenes.heading: Break the notes, the answer breaks

caption.text: A lesion test: break one part, and see if the answer breaks.
Give the talker, which writes the answer, another question's notes: the score falls to 4.19 on familiar questions.
Shuffle the notes between questions: 6.80.
